name: Microsoft REST API Guidelines Evaluation Rubric
description: Comprehensive style rules based on Microsoft Azure REST API Guidelines and Microsoft REST API Guidelines. This profile includes ~120 rules covering versioning, URI design, HTTP semantics, error handling, pagination, long-running operations, naming conventions, security, and more.

categories.name: API Versioning
categories.description: Version management, compatibility, and evolution strategies

options.label: Pass
criteria: api-version query parameter is documented or used in examples
No URI path versioning (e.g., /v1/, /v2/) is present
Version format follows Microsoft conventions (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD-preview)
All api-version values use YYYY-MM-DD format
Preview versions correctly use -preview suffix

options.label: Partial
criteria: api-version is present but format may not follow conventions
Some endpoints missing api-version documentation
Most versions use correct format but some inconsistencies exist

options.label: Fail
criteria: URI path versioning is used
No versioning mechanism is defined
api-version is not documented or required
Semantic versioning (1.0, 2.0) is used
Non-standard date formats are used

categories.evaluationPrompt: Verify that the API uses api-version query parameter for versioning rather than URI path versioning. Check that api-version is documented as a required parameter.

pass.reasoning: Uses correct YYYY-MM-DD format for a GA release.

fail.reasoning: Uses semantic versioning instead of date-based versioning.

categories.name: URI Design
categories.description: Path structure, resource naming, and URL conventions

options.label: Pass
criteria: All collection paths use plural nouns
Singleton resources (if any) are clearly documented

options.label: Partial
criteria: Most paths use plural nouns but some exceptions exist

options.label: Fail
criteria: Collection paths consistently use singular nouns

categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if resource collection paths use plural nouns (users, not user; documents, not document). Individual resources accessed by ID are fine as children of plural collections.

categories.name: HTTP Methods
categories.description: Proper use of GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and other HTTP verbs
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if PUT operations are documented as full replacement. If PUT is used for partial updates, that's incorrect - PATCH should be used instead.

categories.name: Request/Response
categories.description: Payload structure, formats, and content negotiation
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if date and time properties use string type with format 'date-time' (ISO 8601). Look for properties with names like 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'timestamp'.

categories.name: Error Handling
categories.description: Error response format, codes, and troubleshooting

options.label: Pass
criteria: Error responses include error.code (machine-readable)
Error responses include error.message (human-readable)
Error format is consistent across all error responses

options.label: Partial
criteria: Error format is mostly correct but some fields are missing
Error format varies slightly between endpoints

options.label: Fail
criteria: No structured error format is defined
Error responses use non-standard format
Error responses are plain text or unstructured

categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if error responses (4xx, 5xx) use the standard Microsoft error format with error.code and error.message fields.

categories.name: Pagination
categories.description: Collection paging patterns and query options

options.label: Pass
criteria: Collection responses use 'value' array for items
nextLink property is present when more results exist
nextLink is a complete URL

options.label: Partial
criteria: Pagination exists but uses different property names
nextLink format differs slightly from standard

options.label: Fail
criteria: No pagination mechanism is defined
Client-driven page number pagination only

categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if collection responses include a 'nextLink' property for pagination. Collections should return {"value": [...], "nextLink": "url"}.

categories.name: Filtering and Sorting
categories.description: Query parameters for filtering, sorting, and selecting data
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if collection endpoints support $filter query parameter for server-side filtering.

categories.name: Long Running Operations
categories.description: Async operation patterns and status polling

options.label: Pass
criteria: Long-running operations return 202 Accepted
Location header is included for status polling
Status endpoint returns operation progress

options.label: Partial
criteria: 202 is used but Location header format differs
LRO pattern is partially implemented

options.label: Fail
criteria: Long operations block until complete
No async mechanism is defined

categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if operations that may take a long time return 202 Accepted with a Location header for polling.

categories.name: Naming Conventions
categories.description: Property, field, and schema naming standards
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check for consistent naming patterns. For example, if some schemas use 'createdDateTime' and others use 'createdAt', that's inconsistent.

categories.name: Security
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if the security scheme uses OAuth2 (preferably with Azure AD flows). API key authentication alone is not recommended.

categories.name: HTTP Headers
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if responses include a request-id or x-ms-request-id header for request tracing.

categories.name: Schema Design
categories.description: JSON Schema structure and data types
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if schema properties include descriptions explaining their purpose.

categories.name: Collections
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if collection responses use 'value' as the property name for the items array.

categories.name: Conditional Requests
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if GET responses include ETag headers for resources that can be updated.

categories.name: Compatibility
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if the API design avoids patterns that typically lead to breaking changes.
